from PIL import Image
import numpy as np

im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
a = np.asarray(im).astype(float)
# average color per column
col = a.mean(axis=0)  # (1000, 3)

def hue(rgb):
    import colorsys
    r,g,b = [x/255 for x in rgb]
    h,l,s = colorsys.rgb_to_hls(r,g,b)
    return h*360, l, s

# Global stats
print("overall mean RGB:", col.mean(axis=0).round(1))

# Find distinctly blue/cyan columns
blue_cols = []
for i,(r,g,b) in enumerate(col):
    if b > r + 25 and b > 100 and b > g:
        blue_cols.append(i)
    elif b > r + 25 and b > 100:  # cyan-ish
        blue_cols.append(i)
print("columns where blue >> red:", blue_cols[:80], "... total", len(blue_cols))

# Group into runs
runs = []
for i in blue_cols:
    if runs and i - runs[-1][-1] <= 2:
        runs[-1].append(i)
    else:
        runs.append([i])
for r in runs:
    seg = col[r[0]:r[-1]+1].mean(axis=0)
    print(f"blue run x={r[0]}-{r[-1]} avgRGB={seg.round(0)}")

# Brightness profile in 20 buckets
buckets = np.array_split(col, 20)
for i,bseg in enumerate(buckets):
    m = bseg.mean(axis=0)
    print(f"bucket {i:2d} x={i*50}-{(i+1)*50-1}: RGB={m.round(0)} lum={0.299*m[0]+0.587*m[1]+0.114*m[2]:.0f}")

# darkest and brightest single columns
lum = 0.299*col[:,0]+0.587*col[:,1]+0.114*col[:,2]
print("min lum at", int(np.argmin(lum)), lum.min().round(1))
print("max lum at", int(np.argmax(lum)), lum.max().round(1))

# Print color at every 25th column for a sense of progression
for i in range(0,1000,25):
    r,g,b = col[i]
    h,l,s = hue(col[i])
    print(f"x={i:4d} RGB=({r:5.0f},{g:5.0f},{b:5.0f}) hue={h:5.1f} L={l:.2f} S={s:.2f}")

input.content:
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np
import colorsys

im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
a = np.asarray(im).astype(float)
col = a.mean(axis=0)  # (1000,3)
lum = 0.299*col[:,0] + 0.587*col[:,1] + 0.114*col[:,2]

# vertical check: is each stripe flat?
v = a.std(axis=0).mean(axis=1)
print("vertical std within columns: mean=%.2f max=%.2f" % (v.mean(), v.max()))

# hue distribution
hs = []
for rgb in col:
    h,l,s = colorsys.rgb_to_hls(*(x/255 for x in rgb))
    hs.append((h*360, l, s))
hs = np.array(hs)
warm = ((hs[:,0]>=10)&(hs[:,0]<=50)).mean()
green = ((hs[:,0]>60)&(hs[:,0]<170)).mean()
blue = ((hs[:,0]>=170)&(hs[:,0]<=260)).mean()
print(f"fraction warm(10-50deg)={warm:.3f} green(60-170)={green:.3f} blue(170-260)={blue:.3f}")

# dark runs
dark = lum < 18
runs=[]
for i,d in enumerate(dark):
    if d:
        if runs and i-runs[-1][1]<=1: runs[-1][1]=i
        else: runs.append([i,i])
print("dark runs (lum<18):", [(r[0],r[1]) for r in runs if r[1]-r[0]>=1])

# bright runs
br = lum > 150
runs=[]
for i,d in enumerate(br):
    if d:
        if runs and i-runs[-1][1]<=1: runs[-1][1]=i
        else: runs.append([i,i])
print("bright runs (lum>150):", runs)

# print every column 0-100 for start detail
print("\nfirst 40 columns:")
for i in range(40):
    r,g,b = col[i]; print(f"x={i}: ({r:.0f},{g:.0f},{b:.0f})")

print("\ncolumns 930-1000 (ending):")
for i in range(930,1000,2):
    r,g,b = col[i]; print(f"x={i}: ({r:.0f},{g:.0f},{b:.0f})")

# saturation stats
print("\nmean saturation:", hs[:,2].mean().round(3), "mean lightness:", hs[:,1].mean().round(3))

# most saturated columns
sat_order = np.argsort(-hs[:,2])
print("top saturated columns:")
for i in sat_order[:15]:
    r,g,b = col[i]
    print(f"  x={i} RGB=({r:.0f},{g:.0f},{b:.0f}) hue={hs[i,0]:.0f} sat={hs[i,2]:.2f}")

from PIL import Image
im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
# enlarge key regions, stack them with 30px red separators
regions = [(0,110),(150,280),(280,420),(470,570),(690,810),(900,1000)]
crops=[]
for (a,b) in regions:
    crops.append(im.crop((a,0,b,200)))
W = sum(c.width for c in crops) + 30*(len(crops)-1)
H = 200*2  # stack two rows? keep single
out = Image.new('RGB',(W,200),(255,0,0))
x=0
for c in crops:
    out.paste(c,(x,0)); x += c.width+30
out.save('regions.png')
# also a 4x vertical-scaled version of whole strip for viewing
big = im.resize((2000,400), Image.NEAREST)
big.save('big.png')
EOF

from PIL import Image
import numpy as np
import colorsys

im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
col = np.asarray(im).astype(float).mean(axis=0)

def hls(rgb):
    h,l,s = colorsys.rgb_to_hls(*(x/255 for x in rgb))
    return h*360, l, s

green_idx=[]; blue_idx=[]; warm_idx=[]
for i,rgb in enumerate(col):
    h,l,s = hls(rgb)
    if s < 0.05: continue
    if 60<=h<170: green_idx.append(i)
    elif 170<=h<=270: blue_idx.append(i)
    elif 10<=h<=50: warm_idx.append(i)

def runs(idxs):
    out=[]
    for i in idxs:
        if out and i-out[-1][1]<=2: out[-1][1]=i
        else: out.append([i,i])
    return out

print("GREEN runs (hue 60-170, sat>=0.05):")
for r in runs(green_idx):
    seg = col[r[0]:r[-1]+1].mean(axis=0)
    print(f"  x={r[0]}-{r[-1]} len={r[1]-r[0]+1} avg={seg.round(0)} pct={r[0]/10:.1f}-{r[1]/10:.1f}%")

print("\nBLUE runs (hue 170-270, sat>=0.05):")
for r in runs(blue_idx):
    seg = col[r[0]:r[-1]+1].mean(axis=0)
    print(f"  x={r[0]}-{r[-1]} len={r[1]-r[0]+1} avg={seg.round(0)} pct={r[0]/10:.1f}-{r[1]/10:.1f}%")

print(f"\nwarm fraction: {len(warm_idx)/1000:.3f}, green: {len(green_idx)/1000:.3f}, blue: {len(blue_idx)/1000:.3f}")

# luminance profile at 2% resolution
lum = 0.299*col[:,0]+0.587*col[:,1]+0.114*col[:,2]
prof = [lum[i:i+20].mean() for i in range(0,1000,20)]
print("\n2%-bucket luminance profile:")
print(" ".join(f"{p:.0f}" for p in prof))

# r-b difference profile (warmth)
warmth = col[:,0]-col[:,2]
prof2 = [warmth[i:i+20].mean() for i in range(0,1000,20)]
print("\n2%-bucket warmth (R-B) profile:")
print(" ".join(f"{p:.0f}" for p in prof2))

***Puncture*** (released under the title ***Injustice*** in the United Kingdom) is an independent feature film starring [Chris Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Evans_\(actor\) "Chris Evans (actor)"), directed by [Adam Kassen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Kassen "Adam Kassen") and [Mark Kassen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Kassen "Mark Kassen"). The film is based on the true story of [Michael David "Mike" Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_David_Weiss "Michael David Weiss") and Paul Danziger. It was chosen as one of the spotlight films for the 2011 [Tribeca Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival "Tribeca Film Festival"), premiering on April 21, 2011, in New York City.[\[2\]](#cite_note-2)

## Plot

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Puncture_\(film\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")\]

Mike Weiss, a young Houston lawyer and drug addict, and Paul Danziger, his longtime friend and straitlaced law partner, are the personal injury lawyers behind the law firm Danziger & Weiss. They decide to take on a case involving Vicky Rogers, a local ER nurse, who was [pricked by a contaminated needle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Needlestick_injury "Needlestick injury") on the job and contracted HIV. Vicky shows Mike and Paul a [safety needle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safety_syringe "Safety syringe"), invented by her family friend, Jeffrey Dancort, which defends against accidental [needlesticks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Needlestick_injury "Needlestick injury") by only being used once, and she urges them to help bring the product to hospitals. Vicky later dies from her illness. Mike digs deeper into the case, and discovers no one is willing to buy the needle because of a healthcare/pharmaceutical conspiracy and bribery racket. With the threat of exposure, heavyweight attorneys move in on the defense led by attorney Nathaniel Price. Out of their league and out of money, the mounting pressure of the case pushes the two underdog lawyers and their business to the breaking point.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3)

In the meantime, Mike is struggling with his heavy drug usage and his loneliness. He seeks sex therapy as a source of comfort and is consistently in the company of prostitutes. His personal struggles hinder the realization of his professional ambitions, as he misses many of the meetings and investment events, driving a wedge between him and Paul.

Mike, Paul, and Dancort gain the support of Senator O'Reilly, not before she gives Mike an ultimatum: get clean. Mike's heavy withdrawal leaves him hospitalized, only adding to the financial burdens of the firm. The momentum of the case seems to come to a standstill: Senator O'Reilly pulls out after United Medical Health Supplies lobbies for her re-election campaign and Paul, with a new baby at home, is not interested in pursuing the case over his family.

They meet with Nathaniel Price, and he offers a settlement, the tipping point for the conflict between Mike and Paul. Their conflict comes to a head as Mike argues to take the case to trial and seek justice, while Paul protests there is no feasible way they can continue all the way financially. Mike meets a former employee of Thompson Needle Manufacturers and a friend of Vicky's, who implores him to continue the case on behalf of the lives affected by used needles, which spread AIDS and [hepatitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hepatitis "Hepatitis") worldwide. Mike meets with Nathaniel Price and pledges he will personally find new clients and hospital employees affected by these unsafe needles across the country. However, the next day, Paul finds Mike dead from an overdose.

At the settlement conference, Paul walks in with famous personal injury attorney [Mark Lanier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Lanier "Mark Lanier"), declining the settlement and proclaiming that they will see them in court. The movie's postscript tells the audience that in 2004, Attorney Lanier settled a lawsuit against one of the nation's largest medical supply manufacturers for over $150 million.[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) "As a result, thousands of hospitals throughout the United States now use [safety needles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safety_syringe "Safety syringe")."

- Roxanna Hope as Sylvia \- Legal secretary

- [Jennifer Blanc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Blanc "Jennifer Blanc") as Stephany \- Price employee

- [W. Mark Lanier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W._Mark_Lanier "W. Mark Lanier") as himself \- Plaintiff trial attorney

- [Austin Stowell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Stowell "Austin Stowell") as ER Medic

## Production

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Puncture_\(film\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")\]

The original story was written by Danziger. Filming began on February 10, 2010, in [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas "Texas").[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) The film was directed by [Adam Kassen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Kassen "Adam Kassen") and [Mark Kassen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Kassen "Mark Kassen"). Adam Kassen was quoted as saying, "From the moment we heard about this story, we connected to what it says about the current state of our medical industry and the flawed hero that tries to fix it."[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) The director dedicated the film to the real life attorney [Michael David Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_David_Weiss "Michael David Weiss") who died in 1999 of a drug overdose at age 32\.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)

## Release

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Puncture_\(film\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Release")\]

After the film premiered at the 2011 [Tribeca Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival "Tribeca Film Festival"), Millennium Films acquired the distribution rights.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) It had a limited release on September 23, 2011, and played in five theaters. The total domestic gross was $68,945.[\[1\]](#cite_note-mojo-1)

*Puncture* was released on DVD and Blu-ray on January 3, 2012\.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) The film promotes safe needle use worldwide.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)

## Reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Puncture_\(film\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Reception")\]

[Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), a [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator"), reports that 51% of 41 surveyed critics gave the film a positive review, and the average rating was 5\.6/10; the site consensus reads: "There's a compelling story at the heart of *Puncture* but viewers will have to pierce through the formulaic storytelling to find it."[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic") rated it 54/100 based on 17 reviews.[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)

[Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") rated it 3/4 stars and wrote that Evans' performance upstages the issues raised in the film.[\[13\]](#cite_note-:0-13) On Evans' performance, Ebert writes, "Electrifying in the role, Evans reminds me of other great out-of-control druggies played by Al Pacino and Nicolas Cage. A movie like this is a reminder that box-office success can be unfair and limiting to gifted young actors."[\[13\]](#cite_note-:0-13)

Kirk Honeycutt of *[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hollywood_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")* wrote, "The film is chock-a-block with extraordinary performances and no one will fault the filmmaking either. This is a well-made movie, make no mistake. It just suffers from a dysfunctional hero."[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) Ronnie Scheib of *[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_\(magazine\) "Variety (magazine)")* wrote, "Though conceptually intriguing, the mix of downward drug spiral with uphill struggle for good never really coalesces."[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) Jeannette Catsoulis of *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* wrote, "Notable at least in part for its fumbled potential, this health-care-industry melodrama possesses all the right ingredients: an idealistic young lawyer, a corrupt corporate villain and a sympathetic victim. It just fails to assemble them into a compelling whole."[\[16\]](#cite_note-16)

Puncture

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/a/ae/Puncture_Poster.jpg/250px-Puncture_Poster.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Puncture_Poster.jpg) Theatrical release poster

Directed by | [Adam Kassen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Kassen "Adam Kassen") [Mark Kassen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Kassen "Mark Kassen")

Written by | Chris Lopata

Story by | Ela Thier Paul Danziger

Produced by | Adam Kassen Mark Kassen [Jordan Foley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Foley "Jordan Foley")

Starring | [Chris Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Evans_\(actor\) "Chris Evans (actor)") Mark Kassen [Vinessa Shaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinessa_Shaw "Vinessa Shaw") [Brett Cullen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Cullen "Brett Cullen") [Michael Biehn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Biehn "Michael Biehn") [Marshall Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_Bell "Marshall Bell")

Cinematography | Helge Gerull

Edited by | Chip Smith

Music by | Ryan Ross Smith

Production company | [Millennium Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alchemy_\(company\) "Alchemy (company)")

Distributed by | Millennium Entertainment

Release date | - April 21, 2011 (2011-04-21) (Tribeca)

Running time | 99 minutes

Country | United States

Language | English

Box office | $123,700[\[1\]](#cite_note-mojo-1)

***Puncture*** (released under the title ***Injustice*** in the United Kingdom) is an independent feature film starring [Chris Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Evans_\(actor\) "Chris Evans (actor)"), directed by [Adam Kassen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Kassen "Adam Kassen") and [Mark Kassen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Kassen "Mark Kassen"). The film is based on the true story of [Michael David "Mike" Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_David_Weiss "Michael David Weiss") and Paul Danziger. It was chosen as one of the spotlight films for the 2011 [Tribeca Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival "Tribeca Film Festival"), premiering on April 21, 2011, in New York City.[\[2\]](#cite_note-2)

## Plot

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Puncture_\(film\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")\]

Mike Weiss, a young Houston lawyer and drug addict, and Paul Danziger, his longtime friend and straitlaced law partner, are the personal injury lawyers behind the law firm Danziger & Weiss. They decide to take on a case involving Vicky Rogers, a local ER nurse, who was [pricked by a contaminated needle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Needlestick_injury "Needlestick injury") on the job and contracted HIV. Vicky shows Mike and Paul a [safety needle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safety_syringe "Safety syringe"), invented by her family friend, Jeffrey Dancort, which defends against accidental [needlesticks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Needlestick_injury "Needlestick injury") by only being used once, and she urges them to help bring the product to hospitals. Vicky later dies from her illness. Mike digs deeper into the case, and discovers no one is willing to buy the needle because of a healthcare/pharmaceutical conspiracy and bribery racket. With the threat of exposure, heavyweight attorneys move in on the defense led by attorney Nathaniel Price. Out of their league and out of money, the mounting pressure of the case pushes the two underdog lawyers and their business to the breaking point.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3)

In the meantime, Mike is struggling with his heavy drug usage and his loneliness. He seeks sex therapy as a source of comfort and is consistently in the company of prostitutes. His personal struggles hinder the realization of his professional ambitions, as he misses many of the meetings and investment events, driving a wedge between him and Paul.

Mike, Paul, and Dancort gain the support of Senator O'Reilly, not before she gives Mike an ultimatum: get clean. Mike's heavy withdrawal leaves him hospitalized, only adding to the financial burdens of the firm. The momentum of the case seems to come to a standstill: Senator O'Reilly pulls out after United Medical Health Supplies lobbies for her re-election campaign and Paul, with a new baby at home, is not interested in pursuing the case over his family.

They meet with Nathaniel Price, and he offers a settlement, the tipping point for the conflict between Mike and Paul. Their conflict comes to a head as Mike argues to take the case to trial and seek justice, while Paul protests there is no feasible way they can continue all the way financially. Mike meets a former employee of Thompson Needle Manufacturers and a friend of Vicky's, who implores him to continue the case on behalf of the lives affected by used needles, which spread AIDS and [hepatitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hepatitis "Hepatitis") worldwide. Mike meets with Nathaniel Price and pledges he will personally find new clients and hospital employees affected by these unsafe needles across the country. However, the next day, Paul finds Mike dead from an overdose.

At the settlement conference, Paul walks in with famous personal injury attorney [Mark Lanier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Lanier "Mark Lanier"), declining the settlement and proclaiming that they will see them in court. The movie's postscript tells the audience that in 2004, Attorney Lanier settled a lawsuit against one of the nation's largest medical supply manufacturers for over $150 million.[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) "As a result, thousands of hospitals throughout the United States now use [safety needles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safety_syringe "Safety syringe")."

## Cast

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Puncture_\(film\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Cast")\]

- [Chris Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Evans_\(actor\) "Chris Evans (actor)") as Atty. [Michael David 'Mike' Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_David_Weiss "Michael David Weiss") \- Drug addict partner

- [Mark Kassen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Kassen "Mark Kassen") as Atty. Paul Danziger \- Family man partner

- [Marshall Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_Bell "Marshall Bell") as Jeffrey Dancort \- Safetypoint needle inventor

- [Michael Biehn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Biehn "Michael Biehn") as Red \- Vicky's friend and former employee of Thompson Needle

- [Vinessa Shaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinessa_Shaw "Vinessa Shaw") as Vicky Rogers \- Nurse with AIDS

- [Jesse L. Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_L._Martin "Jesse L. Martin") as Atty. Daryl King friend

- [Brett Cullen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Cullen "Brett Cullen") as Nathaniel Price \- Attorney for United Medical group

- [Kate Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Burton_\(actress\) "Kate Burton (actress)") as Senator O'Reilly

- Erinn Allison as Kim Danziger \- Paul's pregnant wife

- Roxanna Hope as Sylvia \- Legal secretary

- [Jennifer Blanc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Blanc "Jennifer Blanc") as Stephany \- Price employee

- [W. Mark Lanier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W._Mark_Lanier "W. Mark Lanier") as himself \- Plaintiff trial attorney

- [Austin Stowell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Stowell "Austin Stowell") as ER Medic

## Production

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Puncture_\(film\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")\]

The original story was written by Danziger. Filming began on February 10, 2010, in [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas "Texas").[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) The film was directed by [Adam Kassen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Kassen "Adam Kassen") and [Mark Kassen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Kassen "Mark Kassen"). Adam Kassen was quoted as saying, "From the moment we heard about this story, we connected to what it says about the current state of our medical industry and the flawed hero that tries to fix it."[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) The director dedicated the film to the real life attorney [Michael David Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_David_Weiss "Michael David Weiss") who died in 1999 of a drug overdose at age 32\.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)

## Release

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Puncture_\(film\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Release")\]

After the film premiered at the 2011 [Tribeca Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival "Tribeca Film Festival"), Millennium Films acquired the distribution rights.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) It had a limited release on September 23, 2011, and played in five theaters. The total domestic gross was $68,945.[\[1\]](#cite_note-mojo-1)

*Puncture* was released on DVD and Blu-ray on January 3, 2012\.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) The film promotes safe needle use worldwide.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)

## Reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Puncture_\(film\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Reception")\]

[Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), a [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator"), reports that 51% of 41 surveyed critics gave the film a positive review, and the average rating was 5\.6/10; the site consensus reads: "There's a compelling story at the heart of *Puncture* but viewers will have to pierce through the formulaic storytelling to find it."[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic") rated it 54/100 based on 17 reviews.[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)

[Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") rated it 3/4 stars and wrote that Evans' performance upstages the issues raised in the film.[\[13\]](#cite_note-:0-13) On Evans' performance, Ebert writes, "Electrifying in the role, Evans reminds me of other great out-of-control druggies played by Al Pacino and Nicolas Cage. A movie like this is a reminder that box-office success can be unfair and limiting to gifted young actors."[\[13\]](#cite_note-:0-13)

Kirk Honeycutt of *[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hollywood_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")* wrote, "The film is chock-a-block with extraordinary performances and no one will fault the filmmaking either. This is a well-made movie, make no mistake. It just suffers from a dysfunctional hero."[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) Ronnie Scheib of *[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_\(magazine\) "Variety (magazine)")* wrote, "Though conceptually intriguing, the mix of downward drug spiral with uphill struggle for good never really coalesces."[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) Jeannette Catsoulis of *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* wrote, "Notable at least in part for its fumbled potential, this health-care-industry melodrama possesses all the right ingredients: an idealistic young lawyer, a corrupt corporate villain and a sympathetic victim. It just fails to assemble them into a compelling whole."[\[16\]](#cite_note-16)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

2006 Australian film

Candy

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/4/40/Candy_%282006%29.jpg/250px-Candy_%282006%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Candy_\(2006\).jpg) Theatrical release poster

***Candy*** is a 2006 Australian [romantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romance_film "Romance film") [drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_\(film_and_television\) "Drama (film and television)"), adapted from [Luke Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Davies "Luke Davies")'s 1997 novel *[Candy: A Novel of Love and Addiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candy:_A_Novel_of_Love_and_Addiction "Candy: A Novel of Love and Addiction")*. *Candy* was directed by filmmaker [Neil Armfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Armfield "Neil Armfield") and stars [Heath Ledger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heath_Ledger "Heath Ledger"), [Abbie Cornish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abbie_Cornish "Abbie Cornish") and [Geoffrey Rush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoffrey_Rush "Geoffrey Rush").

*Candy*, produced by [Margaret Fink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Fink "Margaret Fink"), was released in Australia on 25 May 2006 and subsequently released worldwide.

## Plot

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Candy_\(2006_film\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")\]

There are three acts of roughly three scenes each, [Heaven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heaven "Heaven"), [Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth "Earth"), and [Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hell "Hell").

### Heaven

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Candy_\(2006_film\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Heaven")\]

A poet named Dan and an art student named Candy fall passionately in love, as Candy gravitates to his [bohemian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bohemianism "Bohemianism") lifestyle and love of heroin.

Frequently seeking drug money, they borrow from Candy's parents or eccentric university professor Casper, then turn to theft. When Candy sells her grandmother's ring, she has sex with a pawn shop owner for $50.

### Earth

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Candy_\(2006_film\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Earth")\]

Dan and Candy marry and confront the realities of addiction and family life. Dan purchases the drugs while Candy prostitutes. While considering having sex with men in a park bathroom for money, Dan steals a credit card and scams the owner for his [PIN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_identification_number "Personal identification number"), taking $7000.

Candy becomes pregnant, and despite a few days of tortuously "[going clean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_turkey "Cold turkey")", their baby is delivered stillborn at 23 weeks. They return to heroin, but stop again, enduring agonizing [withdrawal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_withdrawal "Drug withdrawal") symptoms in the process.

Despite poor living conditions, constant struggles for money, and frequent disputes, the pair remain in love.

### Hell

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Candy_\(2006_film\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Hell")\]

Dan and Candy move to the country to "try [methadone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methadone "Methadone")" as a way to ease into a more normal life and eventually quit drugs altogether. After a disastrous attempt to have Candy's parents over for Sunday lunch, Candy screams at her mother about how she is the cause for Candy to "never have been able to unclench \[her\] fists".

After Dan returns home one day from working as a bricklayer, he finds Candy smoking marijuana with a new man and watches as she later leaves to have sex with him. When she returns, she screams at Dan about how much she hates him and wants him to leave. He returns later to find the walls of every room of the house are covered with poems about Dan and Candy that she has written in smeared makeup.

Distressed, Dan seeks Casper again and takes heroin with him. Dan is informed the next morning of Candy's hospitalization back in Sydney, where he finds her in the aftermath of a nervous breakdown. Dan returns to Casper's only to find him dead of a heroin overdose. This forces Dan to reconsider his life.

While Candy recovers in a treatment clinic, Dan gets clean and finds a job washing dishes at a restaurant while still missing Candy. But when Candy finishes treatment and comes to the restaurant to finish off where they started, he cries and says "There's no going back. If you're given a reprieve, I think it's good to remember just how thin it is." She subsequently leaves.

## Cast

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Candy_\(2006_film\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Cast")\]

- [Abbie Cornish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abbie_Cornish "Abbie Cornish") as Candy

- [Heath Ledger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heath_Ledger "Heath Ledger") as Dan

- [Geoffrey Rush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoffrey_Rush "Geoffrey Rush") as Casper

- [Tom Budge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Budge "Tom Budge") as Schumann

- [Tony Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Martin_\(Australian_actor\) "Tony Martin (Australian actor)") as Jim Wyatt

- [Noni Hazlehurst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noni_Hazlehurst "Noni Hazlehurst") as Elaine Wyatt

- [Tim McKenzie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_McKenzie_\(Australian_actor\)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Tim McKenzie (Australian actor) (page does not exist)") as Uncle Rod

- [Tara Morice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tara_Morice "Tara Morice") as Aunt Katherine

- Maddi Newling as Janey

- [Cristian Castillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristian_Castillo "Cristian Castillo") as Little Angelo

- [Paul Blackwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Blackwell_\(actor\) "Paul Blackwell (actor)") as Phillip Dudley

- [Adrienne Pickering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrienne_Pickering "Adrienne Pickering") as bank teller

- [Nathaniel Dean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathaniel_Dean "Nathaniel Dean") as Paul Hillman

- Alicia Hannah as neighbour

- [Anni Finsterer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anni_Finsterer "Anni Finsterer") as Crystal (uncredited)

## Soundtrack

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Candy_\(2006_film\)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Soundtrack")\]

The film features a version of the [Tim Buckley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Buckley "Tim Buckley") song "[Song to the Siren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_to_the_Siren_\(Tim_Buckley_song\) "Song to the Siren (Tim Buckley song)")", sung by actress/singer [Paula Arundell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Arundell "Paula Arundell"). It also includes the track "Sugar Man" from the [debut 1970 album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_Fact "Cold Fact") by Detroit singer-songwriter [Sixto Rodriguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sixto_Rodriguez "Sixto Rodriguez").

## Reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Candy_\(2006_film\)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Reception")\]

On [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), the film holds an approval rating of 47% with an average rating of 5\.76/10, based on 76 reviews. The site's critics consensus reads: "Stars Heath Ledger and Abbie Cornish look better than they should as heroin addicts, and their characters are too absorbed and self-pitying to be totally compelling."[\[1\]](#cite_note-1) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), the film has a weighted average score of 57 out of 100, based on 24 critics, indicating "mixed or average reviews".[\[2\]](#cite_note-2)

[Peter Bradshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Bradshaw "Peter Bradshaw") of *[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")* called it an "excellent, heartfelt film" when compared to [Darren Aronofsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darren_Aronofsky "Darren Aronofsky")'s *[Requiem for a Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Requiem_for_a_Dream "Requiem for a Dream")* and praised both Cornish and Ledger for delivering "performances of absolute conviction".[\[3\]](#cite_note-3) [Geoff Andrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Andrew "Geoff Andrew") of *[Time Out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Out_\(magazine\) "Time Out (magazine)")* felt the film's story was "slightly over-familiar" but gave praise to Armfield's "confident direction" for being "sufficiently fresh and imaginative" and the cast for giving "uniformly strong performances".[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) Russell Edwards of *[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_\(magazine\) "Variety (magazine)")* praised Ledger for giving a "warm depiction" to his role and Armfield for showing restraint in his direction, but critiqued that the script suffers from awkward "behaviour and narrative" shifts, being heavily reliant on the actors, and lacking an "emotional vein" in the ending.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)

- 2006 [Australian Screen Editors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Screen_Editors "Australian Screen Editors") Ellie for Best Editing in a Feature Film [Dany Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dany_Cooper "Dany Cooper") ASE

**Nominated**:

- 2006 Film Critics Circle of Australia: Best Actor in a Leading Role ([Heath Ledger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heath_Ledger "Heath Ledger")), Best Actress in a Supporting Role ([Noni Hazlehurst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noni_Hazlehurst "Noni Hazlehurst")), Best Film, Best Director, Best Adapted Screenplay, Best Music Score ([Paul Charlier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Charlier "Paul Charlier")).

- 2006 [Inside Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inside_Film_Awards "Inside Film Awards"): Best Actor ([Heath Ledger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heath_Ledger "Heath Ledger")), Best Actress ([Abbie Cornish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abbie_Cornish "Abbie Cornish")).

2006 Australian film

Candy

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/4/40/Candy_%282006%29.jpg/250px-Candy_%282006%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Candy_\(2006\).jpg) Theatrical release poster

***Candy*** is a 2006 Australian [romantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romance_film "Romance film") [drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_\(film_and_television\) "Drama (film and television)"), adapted from [Luke Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Davies "Luke Davies")'s 1997 novel *[Candy: A Novel of Love and Addiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candy:_A_Novel_of_Love_and_Addiction "Candy: A Novel of Love and Addiction")*. *Candy* was directed by filmmaker [Neil Armfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Armfield "Neil Armfield") and stars [Heath Ledger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heath_Ledger "Heath Ledger"), [Abbie Cornish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abbie_Cornish "Abbie Cornish") and [Geoffrey Rush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoffrey_Rush "Geoffrey Rush").

*Candy*, produced by [Margaret Fink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Fink "Margaret Fink"), was released in Australia on 25 May 2006 and subsequently released worldwide.

## Plot

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Candy_\(2006_film\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")\]

There are three acts of roughly three scenes each, [Heaven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heaven "Heaven"), [Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth "Earth"), and [Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hell "Hell").

### Heaven

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Candy_\(2006_film\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Heaven")\]

A poet named Dan and an art student named Candy fall passionately in love, as Candy gravitates to his [bohemian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bohemianism "Bohemianism") lifestyle and love of heroin.

Frequently seeking drug money, they borrow from Candy's parents or eccentric university professor Casper, then turn to theft. When Candy sells her grandmother's ring, she has sex with a pawn shop owner for $50.

### Earth

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Candy_\(2006_film\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Earth")\]

Dan and Candy marry and confront the realities of addiction and family life. Dan purchases the drugs while Candy prostitutes. While considering having sex with men in a park bathroom for money, Dan steals a credit card and scams the owner for his [PIN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_identification_number "Personal identification number"), taking $7000.

Candy becomes pregnant, and despite a few days of tortuously "[going clean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_turkey "Cold turkey")", their baby is delivered stillborn at 23 weeks. They return to heroin, but stop again, enduring agonizing [withdrawal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_withdrawal "Drug withdrawal") symptoms in the process.

Despite poor living conditions, constant struggles for money, and frequent disputes, the pair remain in love.

### Hell

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Candy_\(2006_film\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Hell")\]

Dan and Candy move to the country to "try [methadone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methadone "Methadone")" as a way to ease into a more normal life and eventually quit drugs altogether. After a disastrous attempt to have Candy's parents over for Sunday lunch, Candy screams at her mother about how she is the cause for Candy to "never have been able to unclench \[her\] fists".

After Dan returns home one day from working as a bricklayer, he finds Candy smoking marijuana with a new man and watches as she later leaves to have sex with him. When she returns, she screams at Dan about how much she hates him and wants him to leave. He returns later to find the walls of every room of the house are covered with poems about Dan and Candy that she has written in smeared makeup.

Distressed, Dan seeks Casper again and takes heroin with him. Dan is informed the next morning of Candy's hospitalization back in Sydney, where he finds her in the aftermath of a nervous breakdown. Dan returns to Casper's only to find him dead of a heroin overdose. This forces Dan to reconsider his life.

While Candy recovers in a treatment clinic, Dan gets clean and finds a job washing dishes at a restaurant while still missing Candy. But when Candy finishes treatment and comes to the restaurant to finish off where they started, he cries and says "There's no going back. If you're given a reprieve, I think it's good to remember just how thin it is." She subsequently leaves.

## Soundtrack

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Candy_\(2006_film\)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Soundtrack")\]

The film features a version of the [Tim Buckley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Buckley "Tim Buckley") song "[Song to the Siren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_to_the_Siren_\(Tim_Buckley_song\) "Song to the Siren (Tim Buckley song)")", sung by actress/singer [Paula Arundell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Arundell "Paula Arundell"). It also includes the track "Sugar Man" from the [debut 1970 album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_Fact "Cold Fact") by Detroit singer-songwriter [Sixto Rodriguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sixto_Rodriguez "Sixto Rodriguez").

## Reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Candy_\(2006_film\)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Reception")\]

On [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), the film holds an approval rating of 47% with an average rating of 5\.76/10, based on 76 reviews. The site's critics consensus reads: "Stars Heath Ledger and Abbie Cornish look better than they should as heroin addicts, and their characters are too absorbed and self-pitying to be totally compelling."[\[1\]](#cite_note-1) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), the film has a weighted average score of 57 out of 100, based on 24 critics, indicating "mixed or average reviews".[\[2\]](#cite_note-2)

[Peter Bradshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Bradshaw "Peter Bradshaw") of *[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")* called it an "excellent, heartfelt film" when compared to [Darren Aronofsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darren_Aronofsky "Darren Aronofsky")'s *[Requiem for a Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Requiem_for_a_Dream "Requiem for a Dream")* and praised both Cornish and Ledger for delivering "performances of absolute conviction".[\[3\]](#cite_note-3) [Geoff Andrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Andrew "Geoff Andrew") of *[Time Out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Out_\(magazine\) "Time Out (magazine)")* felt the film's story was "slightly over-familiar" but gave praise to Armfield's "confident direction" for being "sufficiently fresh and imaginative" and the cast for giving "uniformly strong performances".[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) Russell Edwards of *[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_\(magazine\) "Variety (magazine)")* praised Ledger for giving a "warm depiction" to his role and Armfield for showing restraint in his direction, but critiqued that the script suffers from awkward "behaviour and narrative" shifts, being heavily reliant on the actors, and lacking an "emotional vein" in the ending.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)

***Half Nelson*** is a 2006 American [drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_\(film_and_television\) "Drama (film and television)") directed by [Ryan Fleck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Fleck "Ryan Fleck") and written by Fleck and [Anna Boden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_Boden "Anna Boden"). The film stars [Ryan Gosling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Gosling "Ryan Gosling"), [Shareeka Epps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shareeka_Epps "Shareeka Epps") and [Anthony Mackie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Mackie "Anthony Mackie"). It was scored by Canadian band [Broken Social Scene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broken_Social_Scene "Broken Social Scene"). 26-year-old Gosling was nominated for the [Academy Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actor "Academy Award for Best Actor") for his performance, becoming the [seventh-youngest nominee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_oldest_and_youngest_Academy_Award_winners_and_nominees#Youngest_nominees_2 "List of oldest and youngest Academy Award winners and nominees") in the category at the time.

The story concerns an [inner city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inner_city "Inner city") [middle-school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle-school "Middle-school") teacher who forms a friendship with a student, after she discovers that he has a drug habit. The film is based on a 19-minute film made by Boden and Fleck in 2004, titled *Gowanus, Brooklyn*.[\[1\]](#cite_note-1) It premiered in competition at the [2006 Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Sundance_Film_Festival "2006 Sundance Film Festival"). It was released theatrically on August 11, 2006\.

## Plot

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Half_Nelson_\(film\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")\]

Dan Dunne is a young middle-school history teacher at a [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn") school, with a teaching style that rejects the standard curriculum in favor of an approach based upon [dialectics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dialectics "Dialectics"). While he is an engaging teacher in the classroom, in his own time he is shown snorting and [freebasing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freebasing "Freebasing") [cocaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocaine "Cocaine"). Dan becomes upset when his ex-girlfriend, Rachel, turns up unexpectedly at a school basketball game, wanting to see him. A short while later, one of his students, Drey, catches him freebasing in the locker room.

Drey's family consists of her overworked single-mother and her brother, Mike, who is in prison for selling drugs for a neighborhood dealer, Frank. Drey's father is also absent, making her dependent on Dan for rides home from school. Her lack of supervision also makes her a target for Frank, who encourages her to sell drugs for him. As Dan and Drey's friendship develops, Dan perceives Frank to be a bad influence on her and tries to persuade him to stay away from her. Drey tries to get Dan to open up about his drug habit to her, though to no avail.

After a tense conversation with Frank about Drey, Dan becomes intoxicated and visits Isabel, another teacher at the school whom he has dated. Initially seeking affection, he then forces himself on her, and she defends herself and runs from him; Dan leaves after apologizing. The following day, Dan is hostile towards Drey, ignoring her concern for him and telling her they are not friends. Drey instead associates with Frank, and completes her first drug sale for him.

Dan goes to his parents' house for dinner, though he is distant and uninterested in the conversation. Dan's brother's girlfriend, Cindy, catches him freebasing in the garage; the two converse and she tells him a joke which makes him laugh. The same night, Drey is out with Frank, selling drugs. Drey arrives at a motel to make a delivery and finds a room of people using drugs. Dan is there and is revealed to be the buyer. The two do not talk as he hands her the money.

The next day, Dan is absent from school, and the class has a substitute teacher. Drey is affected by his absence, and declines a ride home from Frank once school is finished. She instead visits Dan's motel room, finding him hung-over from the previous night. Dan cleans himself up, before sitting down to drink a glass of water. Drey sits down and joins him. The film ends with Dan telling the same joke he heard from Cindy, but he gets the timing of the joke wrong, ruining it. Drey and Dan both break out in laughter at his failed joke.

## Reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Half_Nelson_\(film\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Reception")\]

### Box office

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Half_Nelson_\(film\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Box office")\]

*Half Nelson* was given a [limited theatrical release](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limited_theatrical_release "Limited theatrical release"), opening in two theatres and peaking with 105 theatres.[\[2\]](#cite_note-BOM-2) It grossed $2.7 million domestically (United States and Canada), and $2.2 million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $4.9 million, against a budget of $0.7 million.[\[3\]](#cite_note-NUM-3)

### Critical response

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Half_Nelson_\(film\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Critical response")\]

On the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), 91% of 156 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 7\.6/10. The website's consensus reads: "*Half Nelson* features powerful performances from Ryan Gosling and Shareeka Epps. It's a wise, unsentimental portrait of lonely people at the crossroads. "[\[4\]](#cite_note-Rotten_Tomatoes-4) [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), which uses a [weighted average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean "Weighted arithmetic mean"), assigned the film a score of 85 out of 100, based on 31 critics, indicating "universal acclaim".[\[5\]](#cite_note-Metacritic-5)

On the television show *[Ebert & Roeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/At_the_Movies_with_Ebert_&_Roeper "At the Movies with Ebert & Roeper")* that aired during the weekend of August 13, 2006, [Richard Roeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Roeper "Richard Roeper") and guest critic [Kevin Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Smith "Kevin Smith") gave *Half Nelson* a "two big thumbs up" rating. Smith said that it was probably one of the ten best films he had seen in the last decade.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) Jim Emerson, editor of *[Chicago Sun-Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Sun-Times "Chicago Sun-Times")*, gave the film four-stars-out-of-four and called it a masterpiece.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)

*[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")* film critic Lisa Schwarzbaum awarded the film with an "A" and stated in her review for the film, "*Half Nelson* offers an opportunity to marvel, once again, at the dazzling talent of Ryan Gosling for playing young men as believable as they are psychologically trip-wired."[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) *[LA Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LA_Weekly "LA Weekly")* critic Scott Foundas wrote, "At a time when most American movies, studio made or 'independent,' seem ever more divorced from anything approximating actual life experience, *Half Nelson* is so sobering and searingly truthful that watching it feels like being tossed from a calm beach into a raging current."[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

*[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times")* critic [Kenneth Turan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_Turan "Kenneth Turan") gave the film an enthusiastic response, stating in his review, "What is different about *Half Nelson* is the execution, the kind of subtlety in writing, directing and acting (by costars Shareeka Epps and Anthony Mackie as well as Gosling) you seldom see."[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) Film critic [Jonathan Rosenbaum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Rosenbaum "Jonathan Rosenbaum") of the *[Chicago Reader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Reader "Chicago Reader")* wrote that "a dedicated, charismatic, crack-addicted history teacher is the most believable protagonist in an American movie this year."[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)

*[The Monthly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Monthly "The Monthly")* film critic [Luke Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Davies "Luke Davies") described the film as "engaging and elegant, unpredictable and non-didactic, a film which comfortably sits with its own ambiguities and even allows them to go largely unresolved," commending the film's fresh take on the occasionally exhausted "teacher with a heart of gold" story, achieved by "one of the \[film's\] quiet strengths ... that it doesn't try to resolve Dunne's journey of devouring". Davies concluded that the film's optimistic and pessimistic convergence deemed the film "transparent and sparkling and diamond-hard, a small gem."[\[12\]](#cite_note-12) *[Paste Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paste_Magazine "Paste Magazine")* named it one of the "50 Best Movies of the Decade" (2000–2009), ranking it at \#16.[\[13\]](#cite_note-13)

## Home media

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Half_Nelson_\(film\)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Home media")\]

*Half Nelson* was released on [DVD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DVD "DVD") on February 13, 2007, courtesy of [ThinkFilm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ThinkFilm "ThinkFilm") and [Sony Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Pictures "Sony Pictures").[\[15\]](#cite_note-Amazon.com-15) Bonus features include outtakes, deleted scenes, filmmaker commentary, and a music video by [Rhymefest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhymefest "Rhymefest"). The film has earned $16,180,000 in rentals and $1,538,323 in DVD sales.[\[16\]](#cite_note-The-Numbers.com-16) It was released on [Blu-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blu-ray "Blu-ray") in the United Kingdom in November 2015\.[\[17\]](#cite_note-17)

***Half Nelson*** is a 2006 American [drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_\(film_and_television\) "Drama (film and television)") directed by [Ryan Fleck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Fleck "Ryan Fleck") and written by Fleck and [Anna Boden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_Boden "Anna Boden"). The film stars [Ryan Gosling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Gosling "Ryan Gosling"), [Shareeka Epps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shareeka_Epps "Shareeka Epps") and [Anthony Mackie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Mackie "Anthony Mackie"). It was scored by Canadian band [Broken Social Scene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broken_Social_Scene "Broken Social Scene"). 26-year-old Gosling was nominated for the [Academy Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actor "Academy Award for Best Actor") for his performance, becoming the [seventh-youngest nominee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_oldest_and_youngest_Academy_Award_winners_and_nominees#Youngest_nominees_2 "List of oldest and youngest Academy Award winners and nominees") in the category at the time.

The story concerns an [inner city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inner_city "Inner city") [middle-school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle-school "Middle-school") teacher who forms a friendship with a student, after she discovers that he has a drug habit. The film is based on a 19-minute film made by Boden and Fleck in 2004, titled *Gowanus, Brooklyn*.[\[1\]](#cite_note-1) It premiered in competition at the [2006 Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Sundance_Film_Festival "2006 Sundance Film Festival"). It was released theatrically on August 11, 2006\.

## Plot

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Half_Nelson_\(film\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")\]

Dan Dunne is a young middle-school history teacher at a [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn") school, with a teaching style that rejects the standard curriculum in favor of an approach based upon [dialectics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dialectics "Dialectics"). While he is an engaging teacher in the classroom, in his own time he is shown snorting and [freebasing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freebasing "Freebasing") [cocaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocaine "Cocaine"). Dan becomes upset when his ex-girlfriend, Rachel, turns up unexpectedly at a school basketball game, wanting to see him. A short while later, one of his students, Drey, catches him freebasing in the locker room.

Drey's family consists of her overworked single-mother and her brother, Mike, who is in prison for selling drugs for a neighborhood dealer, Frank. Drey's father is also absent, making her dependent on Dan for rides home from school. Her lack of supervision also makes her a target for Frank, who encourages her to sell drugs for him. As Dan and Drey's friendship develops, Dan perceives Frank to be a bad influence on her and tries to persuade him to stay away from her. Drey tries to get Dan to open up about his drug habit to her, though to no avail.

After a tense conversation with Frank about Drey, Dan becomes intoxicated and visits Isabel, another teacher at the school whom he has dated. Initially seeking affection, he then forces himself on her, and she defends herself and runs from him; Dan leaves after apologizing. The following day, Dan is hostile towards Drey, ignoring her concern for him and telling her they are not friends. Drey instead associates with Frank, and completes her first drug sale for him.

Dan goes to his parents' house for dinner, though he is distant and uninterested in the conversation. Dan's brother's girlfriend, Cindy, catches him freebasing in the garage; the two converse and she tells him a joke which makes him laugh. The same night, Drey is out with Frank, selling drugs. Drey arrives at a motel to make a delivery and finds a room of people using drugs. Dan is there and is revealed to be the buyer. The two do not talk as he hands her the money.

The next day, Dan is absent from school, and the class has a substitute teacher. Drey is affected by his absence, and declines a ride home from Frank once school is finished. She instead visits Dan's motel room, finding him hung-over from the previous night. Dan cleans himself up, before sitting down to drink a glass of water. Drey sits down and joins him. The film ends with Dan telling the same joke he heard from Cindy, but he gets the timing of the joke wrong, ruining it. Drey and Dan both break out in laughter at his failed joke.

## Reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Half_Nelson_\(film\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Reception")\]

### Box office

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Half_Nelson_\(film\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Box office")\]

*Half Nelson* was given a [limited theatrical release](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limited_theatrical_release "Limited theatrical release"), opening in two theatres and peaking with 105 theatres.[\[2\]](#cite_note-BOM-2) It grossed $2.7 million domestically (United States and Canada), and $2.2 million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $4.9 million, against a budget of $0.7 million.[\[3\]](#cite_note-NUM-3)

### Critical response

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Half_Nelson_\(film\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Critical response")\]

On the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), 91% of 156 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 7\.6/10. The website's consensus reads: "*Half Nelson* features powerful performances from Ryan Gosling and Shareeka Epps. It's a wise, unsentimental portrait of lonely people at the crossroads. "[\[4\]](#cite_note-Rotten_Tomatoes-4) [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), which uses a [weighted average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean "Weighted arithmetic mean"), assigned the film a score of 85 out of 100, based on 31 critics, indicating "universal acclaim".[\[5\]](#cite_note-Metacritic-5)

On the television show *[Ebert & Roeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/At_the_Movies_with_Ebert_&_Roeper "At the Movies with Ebert & Roeper")* that aired during the weekend of August 13, 2006, [Richard Roeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Roeper "Richard Roeper") and guest critic [Kevin Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Smith "Kevin Smith") gave *Half Nelson* a "two big thumbs up" rating. Smith said that it was probably one of the ten best films he had seen in the last decade.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) Jim Emerson, editor of *[Chicago Sun-Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Sun-Times "Chicago Sun-Times")*, gave the film four-stars-out-of-four and called it a masterpiece.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)

*[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")* film critic Lisa Schwarzbaum awarded the film with an "A" and stated in her review for the film, "*Half Nelson* offers an opportunity to marvel, once again, at the dazzling talent of Ryan Gosling for playing young men as believable as they are psychologically trip-wired."[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) *[LA Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LA_Weekly "LA Weekly")* critic Scott Foundas wrote, "At a time when most American movies, studio made or 'independent,' seem ever more divorced from anything approximating actual life experience, *Half Nelson* is so sobering and searingly truthful that watching it feels like being tossed from a calm beach into a raging current."[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

*[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times")* critic [Kenneth Turan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_Turan "Kenneth Turan") gave the film an enthusiastic response, stating in his review, "What is different about *Half Nelson* is the execution, the kind of subtlety in writing, directing and acting (by costars Shareeka Epps and Anthony Mackie as well as Gosling) you seldom see."[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) Film critic [Jonathan Rosenbaum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Rosenbaum "Jonathan Rosenbaum") of the *[Chicago Reader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Reader "Chicago Reader")* wrote that "a dedicated, charismatic, crack-addicted history teacher is the most believable protagonist in an American movie this year."[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)

*[The Monthly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Monthly "The Monthly")* film critic [Luke Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Davies "Luke Davies") described the film as "engaging and elegant, unpredictable and non-didactic, a film which comfortably sits with its own ambiguities and even allows them to go largely unresolved," commending the film's fresh take on the occasionally exhausted "teacher with a heart of gold" story, achieved by "one of the \[film's\] quiet strengths ... that it doesn't try to resolve Dunne's journey of devouring". Davies concluded that the film's optimistic and pessimistic convergence deemed the film "transparent and sparkling and diamond-hard, a small gem."[\[12\]](#cite_note-12) *[Paste Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paste_Magazine "Paste Magazine")* named it one of the "50 Best Movies of the Decade" (2000–2009), ranking it at \#16.[\[13\]](#cite_note-13)

## Home media

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Half_Nelson_\(film\)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Home media")\]

*Half Nelson* was released on [DVD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DVD "DVD") on February 13, 2007, courtesy of [ThinkFilm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ThinkFilm "ThinkFilm") and [Sony Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Pictures "Sony Pictures").[\[15\]](#cite_note-Amazon.com-15) Bonus features include outtakes, deleted scenes, filmmaker commentary, and a music video by [Rhymefest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhymefest "Rhymefest"). The film has earned $16,180,000 in rentals and $1,538,323 in DVD sales.[\[16\]](#cite_note-The-Numbers.com-16) It was released on [Blu-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blu-ray "Blu-ray") in the United Kingdom in November 2015\.[\[17\]](#cite_note-17)

from PIL import Image
import numpy as np, colorsys, glob, os

rows = []
for d in ['puncture','candy','halfnelson','infiltrator','bnb2014','boysbrazil']:
    files = []
    if d=='puncture':
        files = sorted(glob.glob('stills/p[1-6].jpg'))
    else:
        files = sorted(glob.glob(f'stills/{d}/*.jpg'))
    stats=[]
    for f in files:
        im = Image.open(f).convert('RGB')
        a = np.asarray(im).astype(float)
        m = a.mean(axis=(0,1))
        h,l,s = colorsys.rgb_to_hls(*(x/255 for x in m))
        lum = 0.299*m[0]+0.587*m[1]+0.114*m[2]
        stats.append((os.path.basename(f), m.round(0).astype(int).tolist(), int(h*360), round(float(lum)), round(float(s),2)))
    rows.append((d, stats))
    print(f"== {d} ==")
    for st in stats:
        print("  ", st)

# build montage per film, thumbnails 120x67
from PIL import Image as I
for d in ['candy','halfnelson','infiltrator','bnb2014','boysbrazil']:
    files = sorted(glob.glob(f'stills/{d}/*.jpg'))
    n=len(files); cols=7; rowsn=(n+cols-1)//cols
    out = I.new('RGB',(cols*120, rowsn*67),(255,255,255))
    for i,f in enumerate(files):
        out.paste(I.open(f).convert('RGB').resize((120,67)), ((i%cols)*120,(i//cols)*67))
    out.save(f'stills/{d}_grid.png')
print("saved grids")
EOF
